_meta.note: center/bbox are population-weighted from GeoNames cities500; bbox is a 0.5–99.5 percentile extent of populated places, omitted for countries spanning the antimeridian. Western Sahara is part of Morocco (MA); GeoNames EH places are read as MA.

AG.name: Antigua and Barbuda
AG.drive_note: These Caribbean islands were a British colony until 1958.

AR.name: Argentina
AR.drive_note: The anniversary on 10 June is still observed each year as Día de la Seguridad Vial (road safety day).

AT.name: Austria
AT.drive_note: Originally LHT, like most of Austria-Hungary, but switched sides after the annexation of Austria by Nazi Germany.

AU.name: Australia
AU.drive_note: British colonies before 1901. Includes Australian external territories.

BA.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
BA.drive_note: Switched sides after the collapse of Austria-Hungary.

BB.name: Barbados
BB.drive_note: This Atlantic island state was a British colony before 1966.

BD.name: Bangladesh
BD.drive_note: Part of Pakistan before 1971, which was part of British India before 1947.

BF.name: Burkina Faso
BF.drive_note: Part of French West Africa before 1958.

BH.name: Bahrain
BH.drive_note: Former British protectorate. Switched to the same side as its neighbours. An island nation, linked by road to the Arabian mainland since 1986.

BI.name: Burundi
BI.drive_note: Belgian colony before 1962. Considering switching to LHT.

BJ.name: Benin
BJ.drive_note: Part of French West Africa before 1960.

BS.name: Bahamas
BS.drive_note: British colony before 1973. Caribbean island. Most passenger vehicles are LHD due to them being imported from the United States.

BZ.name: Belize
BZ.drive_note: British colony before 1981. Switched to same side as neighbours.

CD.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
CD.drive_note: Belgian colony before 1960. RHD vehicles are common, especially in the southeast.

CI.name: Ivory Coast
CI.drive_note: Part of French West Africa before 1960.

CN.name: China
CN.drive_note: Mainland China drives on the right; Hong Kong and Macau keep left-hand traffic (separate entries).

CY.name: Cyprus
CY.drive_note: Under UK administration before 1960. Island nation. De facto divided between the Republic of Cyprus, the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, the UN buffer zone and the British base areas of Akrotiri and Dhekelia. All are LHT.

CZ.name: Czechia
CZ.drive_note: Switched during the German occupation of Czechoslovakia.

DK.name: Denmark
DK.drive_note: Includes the Faroe Islands and Greenland. Danish West Indies were LHT, and continue to be LHT as United States Virgin Islands after US purchase in 1917.

DO.name: Dominican Republic
DO.drive_note: Under Spanish control until 1821 and again from 1861 to 1865.

FJ.name: Fiji
FJ.drive_note: The island nation was a British colony before 1970.

FR.name: France
FR.drive_note: Includes French Polynesia, New Caledonia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Wallis and Futuna, French Guiana, Réunion, Saint Barthélemy, the Collectivity of Saint Martin, Guadeloupe, and Mayotte.

GE.name: Georgia
GE.drive_note: The bus line on Ilia Chavchavadze Avenue runs on the left.

GH.name: Ghana
GH.drive_note: British colony until 1957. Ghana switched to RHT in 1974, a Twi language slogan was "Nifa, Nifa Enan" or "Right, Right, Fourth". Ghana has also banned RHD vehicles – it prohibited new registrations of RHD vehicles after 1 August 1974, three days before the traffic change.

GI.name: Gibraltar
GI.drive_note: Gibraltar is RHT because of its land border with Spain.

GM.name: Gambia
GM.drive_note: British colony until 1965. Switched to RHT on 1 October 1965 being surrounded by the former French colony of Senegal.

GN.name: Guinea
GN.drive_note: Part of French West Africa before 1958.

GR.name: Greece
GR.drive_note: Originally LHT (albeit unofficially) since independence. The establishment of the traffic code switched traffic officially to RHT traffic in 1926.

GS.name: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
GS.geonames_name: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands

GW.name: Guinea-Bissau
GW.drive_note: Portuguese colony until 1974. Drives on the same side as its neighbours.

GY.name: Guyana
GY.drive_note: British colony until 1966. One of the only two countries in continental America which are in LHT, the other being Suriname.

HK.name: Hong Kong
HK.drive_note: kept from British rule, opposite to the mainland

HR.name: Croatia
HR.drive_note: Was then part of the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes.

HU.name: Hungary
HU.drive_note: Originally LHT, like most of Austria-Hungary, but switched sides during World War II.

ID.name: Indonesia
ID.drive_note: Roads and railways were built by the Dutch, with LHT for roads to conform to British and Japanese standards and RHT for railways to conform with Dutch standards. Urban railways also use RHT. Did not change sides, unlike the Netherlands, in 1906.

IE.name: Ireland
IE.drive_note: What is now the Republic of Ireland was part of the United Kingdom before 1922. The Republic covers most of the island of Ireland; the rest of Ireland is part of Northern Ireland, which remains part of the United Kingdom, which is also LHT.

IS.name: Iceland
IS.drive_note: This Atlantic island nation changed to RHT on H-dagurinn. Most passenger cars were already LHD.

JM.name: Jamaica
JM.drive_note: British colony before 1962. Caribbean island. Most passenger vehicles are RHD, tractor-trailers and other heavy-duty trucks are mostly LHD due to being imported from the United States.

JP.name: Japan
JP.drive_note: LHT was enacted in law in 1924. One of the few non-British-colony countries to use LHT. Okinawa Prefecture was RHT from 24 June 1945 to 30 July 1978 because of American rule.

KE.name: Kenya
KE.drive_note: Part of the British East Africa Protectorate before 1963.

KG.name: Kyrgyzstan
KG.drive_note: In 2012, over 20,000 cheap used RHD cars were imported from Japan.

KI.name: Kiribati
KI.drive_note: This Pacific island nation was a British colony before 1979.

KN.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
KN.drive_note: This Caribbean island nation was a British colony before 1983.

KP.name: North Korea
KP.drive_note: Was LHT during the period of Japanese rule. Switched to RHT after the Surrender of Japan.

KR.name: South Korea
KR.drive_note: Was LHT during the period of Japanese rule. Switched to RHT after the USAMGIK Ordinance 65 came into effect.

LA.name: Laos
LA.drive_note: French protectorate until 1953. The First Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge is LHT in connection to Thailand.

LC.name: Saint Lucia
LC.drive_note: This Caribbean island nation was a British colony before 1979.

LS.name: Lesotho
LS.drive_note: British protectorate from 1885 to 1966. Enclave of LHT South Africa.

MA.name: Morocco
MA.drive_note: Under French and Spanish protection until 1956.

MG.name: Madagascar
MG.drive_note: This island nation was a French colony until 1958.

ML.name: Mali
ML.drive_note: Part of French West Africa before 1960.

MM.name: Myanmar
MM.drive_note: British colony until 1948. Switched to RHT under the orders of Ne Win. Theories emerge on the reasoning behind this switch; one claimed that he met an astrologer that recommended him to switch the country's traffic to the right in order to make the nation prosper, while another claimed that international visits caused him to notice that most countries are RHT and so decided to convert the country's handedness of traffic in order to connect Myanmar's roads with other countries' roads in the future.

MO.name: Macau
MO.drive_note: kept from Portuguese rule, opposite to the mainland

MR.name: Mauritania
MR.drive_note: Part of French West Africa before 1960. Mining roads between Fderîck and Zouérat are LHT.

MU.name: Mauritius
MU.drive_note: This island nation was a British colony before 1968.

MV.name: Maldives
MV.drive_note: This island nation was a British colony before 1965.

MZ.name: Mozambique
MZ.drive_note: Portuguese colony until 1975. Drives on the same side as its neighbours.

NA.name: Namibia
NA.drive_note: When South Africa occupied German South West Africa in World War I, it switched to LHT. South West Africa was administered by South Africa 1920–1990.

NE.name: Niger
NE.drive_note: Part of French West Africa before 1958.

NG.name: Nigeria
NG.drive_note: British colony until 1960. Under the military government, it switched to RHT due to being surrounded by RHT former French colonies.

NL.name: Netherlands
NL.drive_note: Includes Aruba, Curaçao, and Sint Maarten.

NP.name: Nepal
NP.drive_note: Shares open land border with LHT India.

NR.name: Nauru
NR.drive_note: This island nation was administered by Australia until 1968.

NZ.name: New Zealand
NZ.drive_note: These Pacific islands, including territories Niue and Cook Islands, were former British colonies.

PG.name: Papua New Guinea
PG.drive_note: After Australia occupied German New Guinea during World War I, it switched to LHT.

PH.name: Philippines
PH.drive_note: Was LHT during the Spanish and American colonial periods. Switched to RHT after the Battle of Manila in 1945. RHD vehicles such as imported buses were still used up until the late 1980s. Philippine National Railways switched to RHT in 2010. Nowadays RHD vehicles are illegal to register and operate for ordinary use under Republic Act 8506 of 1998 however RHD vintage vehicles made before 1960 in "showroom" condition or off-road specialized vehicles are allowed to be used only for motorsports events.

PL.name: Poland
PL.drive_note: South-eastern Poland (former Austrian Partition) was LHT until the 1920s.

PW.name: Palau
PW.drive_note: Palau was under American control until 1986. Most passenger vehicles are RHD due to them being imported from Australia and Japan.

QA.name: Qatar
QA.drive_note: Former British protectorate. Switched to same side as neighbours.

RO.name: Romania
RO.drive_note: Regions of Romania (Transylvania, Bukovina, parts of the Banat, Crișana and Maramureș) that were part of Austria-Hungary were LHT until 1919.

RS.name: Serbia
RS.drive_note: (As part of Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes). Vojvodina was LHT while part of Austria-Hungary.

RU.name: Russia
RU.drive_note: In the Russian Far East, RHD vehicles are common due to the import of used cars from nearby Japan. The railway between Moscow and Ryazan, the Sormovskaya line in Nizhny Novgorod Metro and the Moskva River cable car use LHT.

RW.name: Rwanda
RW.drive_note: Belgian colony before 1962. Considering switching to LHT.

SB.name: Solomon Islands
SB.drive_note: This island nation was a British protectorate before 1975.

SC.name: Seychelles
SC.drive_note: This island nation was a British colony until 1976.

SD.name: Sudan
SD.drive_note: Formerly Anglo-Egyptian Sudan, it switched sides 17 years later to match neighbours.

SE.name: Sweden
SE.drive_note: The day of the switch was known as Dagen H. Most passenger vehicles were already LHD. Railways and the Stockholm Metro did not switch and continue to drive on the left.

SG.name: Singapore
SG.drive_note: This island nation was a British colony until 1963. It was also part of Malaysia until 1965.

SI.name: Slovenia
SI.drive_note: (As part of Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes.) Officially LHT from 1915 as part of Austria-Hungary.

SK.name: Slovakia
SK.drive_note: Switched during the German occupation of Czechoslovakia.

SL.name: Sierra Leone
SL.drive_note: British colony until 1961. Switched to RHT being surrounded by neighbouring former French colonies. Furthermore, it banned the importation of RHD vehicles in 2013.

SN.name: Senegal
SN.drive_note: Part of French West Africa before 1960.

SO.name: Somalia
SO.drive_note: The former British Somaliland had LHT until it formed a union with the former Italian Somaliland which had RHT.

SR.name: Suriname
SR.drive_note: Dutch colony until 1975. One of the only two countries in continental America which are in LHT, the other being Guyana. Did not switch sides, unlike the Netherlands itself.

SZ.name: Eswatini
SZ.drive_note: British protectorate until 1968. Continues to drive on the same side as neighbouring countries.

TG.name: Togo
TG.drive_note: Part of French West Africa until 1960.

TH.name: Thailand
TH.drive_note: One of the few non-British-colony LHT countries. Shares a long land border with RHT Myanmar, Laos and Cambodia.

TL.name: Timor Leste
TL.drive_note: Portuguese colony until 1975. Switched to RHT with Portugal in 1928; following its annexation by Indonesia in 1976, it switched back to LHT, which it has retained since independence.

TN.name: Tunisia
TN.drive_note: RHT was enforced in the French protectorate of Tunisia from 1881 to 1956.

TO.name: Tonga
TO.drive_note: British protectorate before 1970. Polynesian island nation.

TR.name: Turkey
TR.drive_note: Except Metrobus, which is usually LHT.

TV.name: Tuvalu
TV.drive_note: Formerly a British colony. Became independent in 1978.

TW.name: Taiwan
TW.drive_note: Was LHT during the period of Japanese rule. The Republic of China (1912–1949) changed Taiwan to RHT in 1946 along with the rest of China.

UA.name: Ukraine
UA.drive_note: Western parts of the country had LHT under Austro-Hungarian Empire

UG.name: Uganda
UG.drive_note: Part of British Uganda Protectorate from 1894 until 1962.

UY.name: Uruguay
UY.drive_note: Became LHT in 1918, but as in some other countries in South America, changed to RHT in 1945. A speed limit of 30 km/h (19 mph) was observed until 30 September for safety.

VC.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
VC.drive_note: This Caribbean island nation was a British colony before 1979.

VI.name: U.S. Virgin Islands
VI.drive_note: US territory, a rare left-hand one

VN.name: Vietnam
VN.drive_note: French colony until 1954. The Long Bien Bridge uses LHT.

VU.name: Vanuatu
VU.drive_note: Co-administered under France and the United Kingdom until 1980.

WS.name: Samoa
WS.drive_note: Despite New Zealand occupying German Samoa during the first World War, the country did not switch to LHT until 2009; this was for economic reasons, to allow cheaper importation of cars from Australia, New Zealand and Japan.

YE.name: Yemen
YE.drive_note: South Yemen, formerly the British colony of Aden, changed to RHT in 1977, having become one of a few communist countries to use LHT. A series of postage stamps commemorating the event was issued. At that time, North Yemen was already RHT.

ZW.name: Zimbabwe
ZW.drive_note: British colony before 1965 (de facto) or 1980 (de jure).
